decision.section: Iterate — bug: stabilize isolated Playwright suite failures
decision.title: Disposable ownership boundary for mutable E2E
decision.context: Ordinary E2E execution could attach mutating fixtures to an operator's persistent registry when BASE_URL was present.
decision.decision: Run ordinary mutable Playwright projects only through a temporary-home, dedicated-loopback stack and retain live probes as named quarantines.
decision.consequences: Fixture writes are isolated by default; every owner-created project or task must be deleted before its disposable directory is removed.
decision.rationale: A process-local sentinel plus a resolved temporary registry gives the harness an enforceable ownership boundary rather than relying on caller configuration.
decision.rejected: Keeping BASE_URL as an ordinary-suite escape hatch was rejected because it can silently target the operator registry.

changelog.bullet: Isolate mutable Playwright runs in a disposable temporary profile and fail closed when the registry escapes it.
Clean campaign and fixture-owned E2E resources through their API owner paths, including assertion-failure teardown.
Keep genuine live-stack device probes in explicit cleanup-checked quarantine commands.

event_extras.description: Stabilize mutable Playwright fixtures behind a disposable registry boundary.
event_extras.summary: Playwright tests now use their own temporary data and clean it up instead of touching an operator's projects.
event_extras.spec_impact_justification: The change only strengthens the E2E harness and fixture cleanup; Command Center runtime behavior is unchanged.
